extraction.agency_name: Office of the Chief Medical Examiner
extraction.parent_department: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene

findings.title: The Office of the Chief Medical Examiner did not comply with State procurement regulations when purchasing certain medical supplies.
findings.description: OCME purchased medical supplies without competitive bids or written contracts as required by regulation. Review of transactions from May 2011 to May 2014 disclosed $496,000 in purchases from three vendors lacking these requirements.

dollar_amounts.context: repeated purchases for medical supplies from three vendors

findings.recommendation: We recommend that OCME comply with State procurement regulations by soliciting competitive bids and executing written contracts, where applicable (repeat).

extraction.agency_response_summary: The agency concurs with the finding and explains that the Agency Buyer PIN position was abolished and a new one requested but denied. They plan to submit a reclassification request for an existing vacant position by December 31, 2014, and will audit card expenditures to develop contracts where applicable.
